name: JS1/poll-studio
top_fix: Strip the shared React/API/PostgreSQL boilerplate from astraupskill/README.md Prerequisites and VERIFICATION.md Limits (this project has none of those), and rewrite 05-PRACTICE.md exercise bodies with poll-specific acceptance criteria instead of the one repeated paragraph.
summary: Vote preservation moved from array index to stable option ids, and every mutation now goes through a commitPolls() boundary that writes to localStorage before publishing state. Three jsdom tests are genuinely behavioural: they assert id/vote pairing after a row removal, reject case-insensitive duplicate labels, and force Storage.prototype.setItem to throw and verify the saved poll and the in-progress draft both survive. Line ref 'near line 96' is exact and evidence (logs/21-tests.log, 21-browser.png) matches the 3-test claim. Off-stack (no React/Node/SQL) and the practice/solutions chapters are batch template.

name: JS1/kanban-flow
top_fix: Add styles.css rules for the new .move-column select (it was delivered unstyled - styles.css is not in the stage-22 manifest), and replace the shared 05-PRACTICE bodies with board-specific criteria such as 'assert every column's order values form a dense 0..n-1 after any move'.
summary: moveCard was rewritten from an in-place mutator into a validating, immutable, boolean-returning operation that renumbers every column on a copy, persists it, and only then publishes; invalid columns and cross-column beforeIds are rejected and a self-drop is a no-op. Sort ties break on id. Keyboard controls (per-card select plus move up/down) reuse the same function and restore focus, asserted in test 3. Three tests pass per logs/22-tests.log; line ref 'near line 86' is exact. Whole-file CRLF rewrite hides the real diff, and the new select has no CSS.

name: JS1/course-roster
top_fix: Delete the unused realDate helper (server/server.js:113, zero call sites) and collapse the now-unreachable legacy guards at lines 85-95 into the single new gate, so one layer owns each rule; then correct VERIFICATION.md to stop crediting the pre-existing 'enrolled <= capacity' check as part of this change.
summary: Real CRUD lesson: type-gate the body before normalizing, return 409 (not 400) for a uniqueness conflict on a normalized code, and let a record keep its own code when edited (existing.id !== req.params.id). Two tests run real HTTP against the real Express app and cover ASTRA-101 normalization, the 409 on a padded duplicate, a successful title edit, and seven malformed payloads. Astra also fixed a genuinely broken client: index.html loaded App.jsx which never called createRoot, so main.jsx is new. Costs: injected dead code, two overlapping validation layers, and course chapters near-identical to event-admin's (04 differs on 3 of 64 lines).

name: JS1/event-admin
top_fix: Remove the unreachable legacy guards at server/server.js:70-75 (isText/whole at line 67 already excluded those states), keeping only the live cross-field registered<=capacity rule, and fix VERIFICATION.md/01-CODEBASE-MAP.md which credit that pre-existing rule as delivered work.
summary: The strongest single idea in the six Express projects: realDate() round-trips a parsed date back to YYYY-MM-DD, because Date.parse('2027-02-29') silently rolls over to March 1 rather than failing. The type gate correctly runs before normalizeEvent, which would otherwise coerce capacity:'bad' into NaN and lose the reason. Two real-HTTP tests, build and browser checks all verified against checks.json and logs/24-tests.log. Weaknesses: two overlapping validation layers with the older one mostly dead, a pre-existing capacity rule claimed as new, lesson-field-N label ids, and course chapters that differ from course-roster's on a handful of lines.

name: JS1/job-pipeline
top_fix: Add a section to 02-CONCEPTS.md explaining why the '9999-99-99' sentinel at server/server.js:34 is safe (localeCompare on fixed-width ISO strings equals chronological order) and what breaks if the date format changes - a junior will otherwise copy this clever line into a project with MM/DD/YYYY dates. Also delete the unused whole() helper at line 98.
summary: Teaches two list-endpoint staples well: optional fields have three states (absent, deliberately blank, malformed) and must be distinguished, and a sort must be total or items shuffle between requests. The GET route now sorts by nextStepDate with undated records pushed last via a sentinel and ties broken by id. Test 1 asserts the exact ordered projection from a combined search+stage query; test 2 proves four rejected PUTs leave the stored record deepEqual to its pre-edit snapshot. Line ref 'near line 67' exact, 2/2 tests per logs/25-tests.log. Unused helper, lesson-field-N ids, and template chapters 4-7.

name: JS1/stock-catalog
top_fix: Replace the 'Actual implementation excerpt' in 03-WORKED-CHANGE.md: it cites server/server.js line 16 and prints five lines of UNCHANGED pre-existing code (createProductRepository, SORTABLE, a comment) and none of the actual change - not the whole() page/pageSize validation at lines 27-28, not the id tie-break at line 111, not the price/stock gate at lines 64-66. The worked-change chapter contains no worked change.
summary: The most CRUD-relevant domain in the batch - filter, sort, slice one page - and the change fixes the two real bugs: query params were coerced instead of validated (page=Infinity and pageSize=2.5 got through Number(x)||default) and the comparator was not total, so equal-priced items jumped between pages. Test 1 issues the same query twice and deepEquals the id lists, then pages past the end to assert the clamp; test 2 rejects six malformed payloads. Verified against logs/26-tests.log (2/2) and the build entry in checks.json. Also: unused realDate, unreachable legacy guards, and an unexplained logs/26-browser-failure.png beside the clean 'passed' record.

name: JS1/recipe-studio
top_fix: Document the implicit contract the change created: normalizeRecipe dropped its defensive String(item) (server/server.js:91) and now calls item.trim() directly, so it throws a TypeError if ever called without validateRecipe in front of it. Add this to 03-WORKED-CHANGE.md - it is the most valuable teaching point in the change and is currently invisible.
summary: The best nested-data lesson here: the payload contains an array, and the change validates its ELEMENTS (every(x => isText(x,1,500))) before anything mutates, then normalizes by trimming and deduplicating case-insensitively while keeping the user's first spelling ([' Salt ','salt','Water'] -> ['Salt','Water']). Test 2 loops seven malformed payloads including ingredients:[{}] and ingredients:[]. Line ref 'near line 66' exact; 2/2 tests in logs/27-tests.log. Weaknesses: unused realDate helper, unreachable legacy name guard, the stated '1-100' lower bound is actually enforced by a different pre-existing check, and template chapters 4-7.

name: JS1/org-explorer
top_fix: Fix 04-TESTING-AND-DEBUGGING.md:54, where a mechanical template slot-fill produced 'Pause at SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE and inspect input types as well as values' - a Postgres lock mode is not a debugger breakpoint; point at the move handler after BEGIN instead. Then add a project-specific prerequisites note (do course-roster first) and drop the beginner 'an array is an ordered collection of values' paragraph from 01-CODEBASE-MAP.md.
summary: Best course in the batch. A real TOCTOU bug is fixed properly: the move endpoint used to run its cycle check and its UPDATE as two independent pool queries, so two concurrent moves could each pass and together create a cycle. It now BEGINs, takes LOCK TABLE nodes IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE, re-checks node existence, parent existence and the subtree under the lock, updates and commits, with ROLLBACK in catch and release in finally. The test genuinely races two opposing moves with Promise.all and asserts statuses sort to [200,400] plus an acyclic readable tree. 02-CONCEPTS argues the lock's throughput tradeoff honestly. Setup docs and the astra_test_* disposable-schema harness are the best in the batch. 3/3 tests, build and tsc --noEmit all verified in checks.json.

name: JS1/mini-blog
top_fix: Give the project an actual change to teach rather than characterization coverage: add a 404 guard for an unknown parent post on POST /api/posts/:id/comments plus a test that a comment cannot attach to a post deleted between the two calls. Meanwhile delete the two unused helpers (whole and realDate, server/server.js:200-201) and the unreachable legacy branches that 03-WORKED-CHANGE.md currently prints as its worked example.
summary: The domain and the headline test are excellent - a comment created under post A returns 404 when deleted through post B, which is the nested-route authorization mistake real apps ship, and deleting A makes its comment list 404 rather than leaving orphans. But the actual code change is three inserted lines of type gating plus a repair to a React client that never mounted; the cascade and scoping behaviour it teaches already existed, which the report states honestly. Two of the three pasted helpers are dead in this file, the legacy guards are unreachable, and logs/29-browser-failure.png sits unexplained next to a clean 'passed' record in browser-checks.json.

name: JS1/pulse-analytics
top_fix: BLOCKING: the headline worked fixture 'For daily values 10, 0 and 20, the visible moving averages are 10, 5 and 10; cumulative totals are 10, 10 and 30' is wrong and appears in seven files (01:57, 03:13, 04:44, 05:9, 06:13, 07:11, VERIFICATION:18, the last under the heading 'Tested behavior'). test/feature.test.ts:9 uses 10/0/30 and asserts MA [10,5,13.33] and cumulative [10,10,40]. 07-TRACE-LAB even contradicts itself: line 11 says 10,5,10 and the table at line 19-22 says 10,5,13.33. Find-and-replace the fixture everywhere, then re-read chapter 7.
summary: The SQL change is one of the two best in the batch: a GROUP BY only emits groups present in the data, so the old 7-day moving average was computed over existing rows rather than calendar days. The rewrite builds a generate_series calendar spine, LEFT JOINs daily_metrics, COALESCEs to zero and only then applies the window functions; the summary route's off-by-one window bound was fixed to match. The test asserts exact revenue/cumulative/MA/delta arrays against real Postgres in a disposable per-run schema, and setup docs are the most followable in the batch. REWORK is triggered solely by D1=2 for the contradictory fixture - the fix is small and this becomes core-path material afterwards.
